The test image shows a lodged/fallen corn plant with scattered small brown spots on leaves and a dried ear visible. This is a whole_plant view. Key candidates from whole_plant category: Physoderma_Stalk_Rot (plants break at nodes), Physoderma_Brown_Spot (spots on leaves + stalk involvement), Bacterial_Stalk_Rot (sudden collapse).

The scattered small brown spots on leaves strongly suggest Physoderma_Brown_Spot. Let me check one reference.

The Physoderma_Brown_Spot reference shows very characteristic small yellow-to-orange-brown spots in banded pattern across the leaf with distinct dark oval spots on the midrib. The test image shows scattered brown spots on leaves and a lodged/collapsed plant.

Comparing:
- The scattered brown spots on leaves in the test image are consistent with Physoderma Brown Spot, though not as distinctly banded as the reference
- The lodged/fallen plant is consistent with the stalk involvement aspect of Physoderma (same pathogen can cause both Physoderma_Brown_Spot and Physoderma_Stalk_Rot)
- Physoderma_Brown_Spot is listed under leaf, stem, AND whole_plant categories, consistent with this multi-part presentation
- The dark spots visible on some midribs/leaf sheaths in the test image align with the characteristic midrib spots

The combination of scattered leaf spots + plant lodging points to Physoderma complex, with Brown Spot being the more complete diagnosis covering the leaf symptoms visible.
